scope: Protected remote actor channels for the authoritative world runtime
invariant: Remote actors prove their own identity over protected transport and use the same world authority and actor handlers as local actors.
current_evidence: prepare_actor_channel currently accepts only inherited unnamed AF_UNIX sockets.
worldd currently requires identity configuration and inherited actor descriptors together.
IdentitySessions currently requires one through 32 inherited actor channels.
The issuer already has a bounded TLS 1.3 listener and private TLS material loader.
No existing issuer listener qualifies remote world actor transport.
required_evidence: Explicit protected listener configuration; no network access to trusted management operations
Trusted server authentication and fresh actor proof; transport credentials alone grant no actor authority
Rejected plaintext, untrusted peers, mismatched server identity, replayed proofs, and cross-channel proofs
Real authenticated actions through the existing world authority and actor engine
Shared persistent world actors connected from both sb16 and sb16-2
No workspace creation, selection, or authority granted by connection or world admission
Bounded handshakes, connections, frames, partial writes, and slow peers
Controller disconnect and credential revocation cancel motion and affected control while other valid actors continue
World restart invalidates old sessions and proofs while preserving durable actor context
Independent Debug and runtime sanitizer qualification on both hosts with the complete baseline
implementation_constraints: Keep the trusted management pipe separate from remote actor traffic.
Reuse the production WorldSessionRequest and WorldSessionReply protobuf interface.
Do not relay the management interface or create a second actor engine.
Keep TLS private material outside workspace data and Git.
Preserve local actor channels and existing authorization checks.
Do not add remote application streaming or remote application input to M1 scope.
Record interface changes before implementation. Keep locked acceptance assertions unchanged.
limitations: This task records a verified implementation gap. It has no passing remote-world evidence yet.
Transport qualification alone does not complete shared-world persistence, world transitions, or M01.
Issuer revocation acknowledgement still does not prove a distributed cancellation barrier.
